title: How long does a digital twin of a chaotic system stay accurate? Each e-fold of smaller state error buys 1.12 time units on Lorenz-63 (1/lambda = 1.11)
summary: Runs a Lorenz-63 truth and a twin together and measures the mean time (40 attractor start points) until they are 1.0 apart. The measured largest Lyapunov exponent is 0.904 (published 0.9056). With exact parameters, the horizon grows 1.124 time units per e-fold of smaller initial-state error (4.1 at 10<sup>−2</sup>, 16.9 at 10<sup>−7</sup>), close to 1/λ but about one unit below ln(tol/d<sub>0</sub>)/λ. A relative parameter error in ρ with exact start gives 0.95 at 10<sup>−2</sup> and 7.8 at 10<sup>−5</sup>, and gains about 1/λ per e-fold too (1.00 without the saturated 10<sup>−1</sup> row; an earlier 0.85 was a fit-range artefact): it costs a constant, not a slope. One system, one tolerance; only the mean is reported; the explanation of the offset is not tested. Parameters are Lorenz’s; the tolerance is chosen.
lede: how long does a digital twin of a chaotic system stay accurate? On Lorenz-63 each e-fold of smaller state error buys 1.12 time units (1/lambda = 1.11); a parameter error costs a constant offset with the same slope. Mean over 40 starts, one tolerance.
